market_holds: No usable option chain (ATM spread 140% of mid), so the usual move is the median of the last 7 reactions, 7.01% (max 15.44%), 3 up in 7 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-17). Consensus for fiscal Q4 (ended 2026-09-26) is thin and inconsistent: $1.21 EPS / $400.5M revenue per Earnings Whispers (2026-11-10), $1.22 and $1.31 on Benzinga pages, $1.38 on FXEmpire (4 analysts), against $1.58 a year ago; coverage is about 2-4 analysts (Jefferies upgraded to Buy, PT $101, 2026-08-06; Benchmark Buy). No formal numeric guide: management said Q4 sales should improve as bakery drag eases, organic growth more likely from Q1 FY27, freight/fuel pressure persisting into Q4, Apollo savings running ahead ($20M plant run-rate, $25M program). Run-in: JJSF about 76.5 (2026-09-30) to about 90.2 intraday on the run day (+16-18%), almost all of it alongside consumer staples (XLP 80.6 to 91.8, +14%) while SPY fell about 6%; relative to XLP the stock is only about +3.5% (Yahoo daily bars). Earnings Whispers' preview says the expectations bar has risen even though the consensus EPS looks undemanding. Short interest unknown.
view: The Q4 numbers probably beat the stale consensus EPS. Fiscal Q4 lines up almost exactly with calendar Q3, and the high-margin theater ICEE channel had a strong quarter: AMC domestic attendance up about 23% and Cinemark US/Canada attendance up 12.7%, both well above the +9% box office management had projected for this period a year ago. A year earlier the same quarter was hit by an 11% box-office decline. Apollo plant savings (about $5M a quarter) roughly offset the freight hit (about $5M a quarter, with diesel averaging $5.43 in the quarter against $3.75 a year ago, about the same as Q3). Sysco's local case volume, +2.7% over the identical 13 weeks, says foodservice demand held. My own rebuild puts adjusted operating income near $34-36M and EPS near $1.30-1.45, against the $1.21-1.31 most aggregators show. The company also beat in the same quarter last year ($1.58 vs $1.19) and beat Q3 by about 9.5%. Against that, this stock has reacted to sales and tone as much as to EPS: the big Q4 FY25 beat came with a revenue miss and closed only +1.1%, and the Q2 FY26 beat with falling sales closed -7%. Q4 revenue is likely only near the $400M consensus, because bakery rationalization still takes about 2.5 points and machine and service sales were falling $10M a quarter in Q3. The forward line is the bigger risk. Diesel averages $6.22 in the current quarter (Q1 FY27), against about $3.7 a year ago and above Q4's level, so the call's FY27 commentary on freight could temper the 'return to growth' pledge. Meanwhile the stock has rallied 16% with defensive staples. Net: a modest lean up on the print. It is not a mechanism I would bet on at 65%.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the theater rebound in ICEE beverage volume: thinly covered estimates that are about 100 days old, centred near $1.21-1.31 (down about 20% year on year), look anchored on management's cautious August tone and the +9% box-office assumption rather than on the counterparties' reported +13-23% attendance. But the price has already moved 16% (mostly with staples), and the forward freight shock is visible to everyone, so I cannot show a gap large enough to act on.

recommendation.reason: Counterparty data (AMC, Cinemark attendance; Sysco volume) and Apollo savings make an EPS beat against a stale, thin consensus more likely than not. This stock's reaction has turned on sales and outlook tone, though, and both are exposed: revenue probably only near consensus, and FY27 freight with diesel above $6. A run-up with the staples sector also leaves less room. The probability does not reach the 65 needed to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Frozen Beverages line showing double-digit beverage growth, with revenue at or above $405M and FY27 commentary that says Apollo savings and pricing/surcharges cover freight, would push this to a clear long. A Q4 sales decline worse than 3%, or FY27 language walking back growth because of fuel, would make it a short.

self_critique: The theater rebound and the record summer were very public: Cinemark and AMC reported records in early November, and JJSF rose 4.6% on 2026-11-04. The whisper number is likely above $1.31, so a modest beat may already be expected. Diesel above $6 into FY27, falling machine and service sales and the bakery drag could produce a revenue miss and a cautious FY27 tone, which is the pattern that produced -7% and -15% reactions this year. The 16% rally with staples leaves less room, and the stock is up 2% on the run day itself.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: the rally is the staples rotation, not company news. Counterparty data (theater chains, Sysco on the identical window) gave the most decisive inputs. P7's push to estimate the line from inputs was useful, but the outlook tone remains unknowable here, so it stayed a lean.
